newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prodi says Italy needs efforts to meet EMU - paper.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Italy needs efforts to meet EMU - paper.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said his country still needed to make great efforts to meet the criteria to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU), a German newspaper reported on Tuesday.
"Italy has much bigger economic problems than Germany and great efforts are necessary to make our country fit for Maastricht," Prodi said in an interview with Die Zeit.
In a transcript of the interview released ahead of the Thursday publication, the newspaper quoted Prodi as saying central banks must remain independent.

Asked if it would not be best to delay the start of monetary union from its scheduled January 1999 date, as Germany may exceed the Maastricht deficit goal while Italy comes closer to meeting it, Prodi said, "I don't see it that way. ... If others want to delay, we will think about this possibility. But Italy alone will not seek (a delay).
"We stand by the criteria, without fiddling around, without tricks or creative bookkeeping."

Asked about his stand on the Franco-German debate on the need for a political counterweight to central banks' independence, Prodi said, "I hold the independence of the central bank as indispensable, as in Germany and in Italy, where ... the independence is even stronger."

Prodi said Italy was coming very close to bringing its budget deficit down to 3.0 percent of gross domestic product, from 6.9 percent last year, thanks mainly to lower interest rates and a surplus in its primary budget before debt service.
Prodi said he did not share the glee some others are taking in the prospect that Germany's deficit might exceed the three percent guideline this year.
Germany can meet the deficit target if it tries, he said. "The Germans can make it. If not, it is a political decision. German has the choice."
Prodi said Germany should stand more decisively for Europe. "Without a certain measure of German leadership, Europe will fall into a deep crisis ...
"German society is in this question more sharply divided than Italy. The decision about European monetary union must be made quickly. And for that, German leadership is needed."
Prodi said that unless Italy reduces its debt it has no chance to become a modern society, but that membership in EMU was part of his clear strategy toward that goal.
"Italy fits well in the currency union under the existing criteria," he said.
